transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Kapoor (Nimbus Lead Eng), Jonas Li (Nimbus CTO), Rita Gomez (PM), Evan (SRE)

Summary: quick pass on SDK integration pain points, review of last week's sample run, discuss structured output schema mismatches, plan a focused latency/cost benchmark with KV cache and batching toggles, and agree next steps for security docs and network prep.

Topics: SDK usage patterns; function/tool-calling failure modes; structured JSON output validation; KV cache mis-samples; VPC peering questions; SOC2/KMS concerns.

—— Transcript ——
[00:00] Alex (AE): All right, thanks everyone for joining, we'll kick off. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Maya: Hey, Maya here.
[00:06] Jonas: Jonas on the call.
[00:08] Rita: Rita.
[00:09] Evan: Evan, SRE.
[00:11] Samir (SE): Samir here. Cool.

[00:15] Alex: Great, last week we shipped the SDK sample and the structured-output spec, couple of you tried the sample. Maya you filed the bug list — can you quickly run through the top two?
[00:28] Maya: Yeah. So first, the model sometimes returns an array where we expected an object, so our parser dies. I think it's the function-calling wrapper — sometimes the tool call arrives with a stray comma or the model adds commentary around the JSON like so, "note: this is approximate" and that trips the schema validator.
[00:46] Samir: Hmm, we saw that in internal tests when the model has low temperature; sorry, high temperature, so more creative outputs. We can force the SDK's output_mode to "strict-json" which will wrap the final tokenization and try a second parse pass, but it's not perfect. There's also the function-calling path — if the model emits text plus a function payload, the SDK currently does best-effort extraction.
[01:10] Jonas: Is that a Redwood runtime thing or a model behavior we can tame?
[01:13] Samir: A bit of both. The runtime will prefer the function-calling channel when the assistant token stream signals it, but even then some models interleave commentary. Our recommendation: pin model variant used in pilot and use the SDK's pre-processor to strip leading commentary. Also lower temperature for production-like runs.
[01:35] Rita: For acceptance, we need >99% parse success on our 1000 sample prompts. Any idea how far off we are?
[01:42] Maya: With current sample set we saw ~95% pass, the rest are either extra text or schema key mismatches (e.g., "patient_name" vs "name").
[01:51] Alex: Ok that's actionable: Samir will run a bench with the 1k sample set and toggle the SDK strict-json and also run with KV cache enabled/disabled. That should show impact on both success rates and latency.

[02:10] Samir: Another note — on KV cache (we sometimes call it KV cash in older transcriptions — ha) when you have multi-turn recalls the response is faster but you have to be careful with stale keys for PII-related fields. We recommend a TTL strategy and explicit cache invalidation when the app edits a record.
[02:34] Evan: For us, data residency and audit is bigger: we need to ensure the KV store doesn't persist plaintext PHI in a way that violates our policy. How does Redwood handle encryption at rest for the cache?
[02:45] Samir: Current setup encrypts content at rest via customer-managed KMS when using Private or Dedicated. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS for enterprise tenants. I'll attach the KMS flow diagram.
[02:59] Jonas: Great. Also, on the network side, what's required for VPC peering? Do we need static egress, or is there a load-balanced egress set?
[03:08] Alex: For Private customers we do VPC peering and you get fixed endpoints; for Hosted, we have a NAT egress pool — if you need fixed egress we can do dedicated tenancy or a reserved IP pool as part of Dedicated. Evan, we should sync offline to map your firewall rules.
[03:23] Evan: Yep will do, we'll share the diagram.

[03:30] Maya: Back to structured-output: sometimes the function calling returns nested arrays and our UI doesn't support that. Is there a way to enforce a flattened schema from the model?
[03:40] Samir: You can add a post-process step in the SDK schema adapter to normalize arrays to either first-element-only or to a delim pattern. We can provide a sample normalization helper in the repo.
[03:51] Maya: That would help. Also on token cost — we're seeing wide variance depending on prompt preambles and system messages. Can Redwood advise on trimming strategies?
[04:01] Alex: Yes — one thing is prefix/KV caching: store stable system messages in cache and only send deltas. Also suggested is model quantization and a smaller context model for bulk summarization. Samir can propose models + quant profiles after the bench.
[04:16] Samir: I'll include two config profiles: conservative (lower cost, slightly higher latency) and performance (lower latency, higher cost), and show token estimates on the bench.

[04:30] Rita: Any gotchas with the SDK when we do function chaining — i.e., call tool A then B with state?
[04:38] Samir: The main issue is KV cache coherence and ensuring the runtime maintains a consistent KV store per convo session. We recommend the SDK session token map; also for long chains, streaming responses can help UX but you must handle partial outputs.
[04:52] Maya: We saw a case where streaming cut a JSON mid-structure and the front-end parsed partial JSON which crashed. Is there an SDK utility to buffer and only emit complete JSON objects?
[05:02] Alex: Yes, the SDK stream consumer has an "emitOnComplete" flag — default false. We'll surface that in the sample repo and set true for schema-driven endpoints.

[05:12] Jonas: Security wise, we need SOC2 docs and a list of infra subcomponents for our audit team.
[05:18] Alex: I'll drop the SOC2 summary and infra notes into the CRM, and attach KMS integration docs as mentioned. Expect that by Monday.
[05:25] Rita: Good. For acceptance criteria, besides parse success, we need 99th percentile latency < 750ms for single-turn summarizations in our staging region. Is that feasible on hosted?
[05:35] Samir: For hosted it's plausible if you pick a lower-latency model and enable prefix caching. But if you need strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated with pinned GPU pools. Our bench will include P99 numbers both hosted and simulated dedicated.
[05:51] Evan: One more on cost: can you show per-route token breakdowns? We want to attribute spend per feature.
[05:57] Alex: Console does per-route cost breakdown — we'll set up a temporary view for your pilot team. I'll send the invite to your team.

[06:10] Maya: Quick note — we tried the function-calling example and sometimes the SDK lost the function name when model emitted aliases (e.g., "updatePatient" vs "update_patient"). Any suggestions?
[06:22] Samir: Normalize function names server-side with a mapping table; SDK has a name-alias option but we can demonstrate best practices in the sample code.

[06:35] Jonas: Ok wrap up — let's recap action items and owners.
[06:38] Alex: Sure — Alex will share checklist + repo; Samir will run the 1k bench with toggles (strict-json, KV on/off, streaming vs non-stream); Maya provides the 10 representative prompts and the 1k sample set; Evan shares network diagram. We'll reconvene next Friday same time to review bench results.
[06:58] Rita: Can we add a small spike to test Dedicated boot time if we request a short reserved pool? It helps our infra planning.
[07:05] Samir: Yes we can schedule a smoke Dedicated pool for a day; I need to check capacity but will flag it as part of the bench request.

[07:15] Alex: Thanks everyone. I'll post notes and next steps. Meeting adjourned.

Notes about transcription: occasional misattributions and small words missing; "VPC" sometimes transcribed as "VCP" in the raw. We preserved filler words and brief crosstalk.

End of transcript.
